page: Amazon Web Services hpc6id.32xlarge is an x86_64 high-performance computing instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor providing 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, backed by 54 MB of L3 cache and support for AVX-512 vector extensions. The instance is equipped with 1024 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, 15,200 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, and a 200 Gbps baseline network interface. It operates without discrete GPUs.

Benchmark results show top-tier execution across high-throughput and vector-heavy compute tasks. The instance placed in the top 10% for Clang compilation (61,729.0), multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (564.52 GB/sec), and PassMark extended CPU instructions (115,109.02). Multi-core throughput is strong, reflected in a stress-ng multi-core score of 121,141.14 and a PassMark CPU score of 79,173.37. Memory subsystems registered 339.55 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 141.28 GB/sec write bandwidth. Conversely, single-threaded metrics remain within average bands, with stress-ng single-core (1,894.3) and Geekbench single-core (1,692.0) pacing typical server-grade Xeon silicon.

Cost efficiency is driven by high resource consolidation. By pairing 64 dedicated non-hyperthreaded cores with 16 GB of memory per core, extreme NVMe capacity, and 200 Gbps networking, the instance reduces the need to distribute memory- or I/O-intensive datasets across multiple smaller nodes. However, workloads constrained strictly by per-core clock speed or single-thread performance will underutilize its physical core density and wide interconnect.

The hpc6id.32xlarge is engineered for finite element analysis, computational fluid dynamics, large-scale software compilation, distributed memory databases, and intensive I/O data pipelines requiring fast local scratch space.

Configured with 1024 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, it delivers 16 GB of RAM per core without hyperthreading overhead. Storage and networking capabilities include 15,200 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD space and a 200 Gbps network interface, running without hardware GPU acceleration. Benchmark evaluations show top-decile ratings in parallel software compilation, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and AVX-512 extended instruction processing, alongside strong multi-core and memory bandwidth execution. Single-core performance sits in the middle tiers. This instance is structured for distributed scientific modeling, computational fluid dynamics, high-throughput caching, and large batch compilation pipelines.
